newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: 17 N.Koreans seek asylum in S.Korea, biggest defection.
newsitem.headline: 17 N.Koreans seek asylum in S.Korea, biggest defection.

text.p: Seventeen North Koreans have fled to Hong Kong seeking asylum in South Korea in the biggest-ever mass defection from the communist country, a Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
In an international escape that involved helpers in China and the United States, the group travelled under cover for nearly one month through China before arriving in Hong Kong on November 23.
All but one of group, which included five children and a pregnant woman, are relatives. The other defector is a North Korean security official, the spokesman told reporters.
It would be the largest ever group defection to South Korea from the communist North.
The previous largest defection was in 1987 when North Korean doctor Kim Man-chol, his wife and nine other relatives came to the South via a third country.
The 17 sneaked into China on October 26 and crossed into Hong Kong on November 23. They are now being held in a refugee centre in Hong Kong, the spokesman said.
They were helped by ethnic Koreans in China, who were paid to act as guides by relatives of the North Koreans living in the United States, he said.
One of the defectors is the daughter of Choi Young-do, a defector now living in the United States, he added.
Seoul officials said the 17 are the latest of a growing exodus of North Koreans fleeing hunger and grinding poverty in recent years.
A total of 34 North Koreans, excluding the present 17, have so far defected from the Stalinist state to South Korea this year. There were 38 defections last year and 50 in 1994.
Among North Koreans who have sought asylum this year were a pilot who flew his MiG-19, a diplomat at North Korea's Zambian embassy, a scientist and a drama script writer.
